activity.notes: Representative year 356 BCE marks the first major round of Shang Yang's reforms in Qin. ATLAS records a bounded reform milestone rather than fabricating a lifespan-scale office rail.

sources.title: Institutional Reforms and Reformers during the Warring States Period — The Oxford Handbook of Early China
sources.citation_text: Yuri Pines describes the Qin reforms associated with Shang Yang as replacing pedigree-based order with ranks of merit and deepening centralization and bureaucratization, strengthening Qin's capacity to mobilize resources.

sources.title: National integration and institution building — Pacific Economic Review
sources.citation_text: The article dates the start of Shang Yang's two rounds of Qin institutional reforms to 356 BCE and summarizes their administrative, military-merit, county, land, and measurement reforms.
